senses.gloss: An official who enforces hunting, fishing, and wildlife laws in an area.
examples: A game *warden* checked our fishing licenses at the boat ramp.
The *warden* fined him for shooting out of season.
Two *wardens* patrol the whole state forest.

senses.gloss: Friendliness and kind feeling toward other people.
examples: She greeted every guest with real *warmth*.
There was no *warmth* in his voice at all.
I still remember the *warmth* of that welcome.

senses.gloss: An official caution given instead of a punishment, telling someone not to do it again.
examples: The officer let me off with a *warning*.
He got a written *warning* from his manager.
One more *warning* and you're off the team.

senses.gloss: A bend or twist in something that should be flat or straight.
examples: There's a slight *warp* in the tabletop.
Damp air put a *warp* in the door, and now it sticks.
Sight down the board and check it for *warp*.

senses.gloss: A situation in which gains and losses cancel out, leaving no real change.
examples: After the new fees, the raise was basically a *wash*.
We saved on gas but paid more for parking, so it was a *wash*.
For the company the whole quarter came out a *wash*.

senses.gloss: A machine that washes clothes.
examples: The apartment comes with a *washer* and dryer.
Don't put that sweater in the *washer*.
Our *washer* leaked all over the basement floor.

senses.gloss: The careless or pointless use of something valuable such as time, money, or talent.
examples: That meeting was a complete *waste* of time.
Leaving the lights on all night is such a *waste*.
It's a *waste* of good food to throw it out.

senses.gloss: A period of time spent guarding a place or looking out for danger.
examples: The sailors stood the night *watch* in shifts.
Someone has to keep *watch* while the others sleep.
He had the four-hour *watch* on deck.

senses.gloss: An official alert that dangerous weather is possible in an area.
examples: The county is under a tornado *watch* until nine.
A flash flood *watch* covers most of the valley.
A *watch* means get ready; a warning means take cover.

senses.gloss: A movement of the raised hand used to greet someone or say goodbye.
examples: She gave us a quick *wave* from the car.
He said goodbye with a *wave* and walked off.
A friendly *wave* from a neighbor made her whole day.

senses.gloss: A sudden increase in something that spreads through a place or a group.
examples: A *wave* of layoffs hit the whole industry.
The city is bracing for another heat *wave*.
*Waves* of protesters filled the square.

senses.gloss: A form in which energy such as sound, light, or a radio signal travels.
examples: Sound *waves* travel faster through water than through air.
Radio *waves* carry the signal to the tower.
Doctors use sound *waves* to look at the baby.

senses.gloss: Clothing of a particular kind, especially as sold in stores.
examples: The store's children's *wear* is on the second floor.
She designs evening *wear* for a small label.
Formal *wear* is required at the dinner.

senses.gloss: An informal word for a sneaky, dishonest person you cannot trust.
examples: That *weasel* took credit for my work.
Don't be a *weasel* — just tell her the truth.
The landlord is a *weasel* about returning deposits.

senses.gloss: Lengths of extra hair sewn or glued into a person's own hair.
examples: She got a *weave* before the wedding.
A good *weave* can last a couple of months.
The salon does braids, *weaves*, and color.

senses.gloss: The system of linked pages and sites on the internet.
examples: You can find the form on the *web*.
He spent all afternoon searching the *web*.
The article is only on the *web*, not in print.

senses.gloss: A thick triangular piece cut from something such as cheese, cake, or fruit.
examples: She cut the lime into *wedges*.
He ordered a *wedge* of apple pie.
Serve the potato *wedges* with sour cream.

senses.gloss: A slang word for marijuana.
examples: The whole car smelled like *weed*.
*Weed* is legal in a lot of states now.
He quit smoking *weed* in college.

senses.gloss: The importance or influence that something or someone has.
examples: Her opinion carries a lot of *weight* around here.
The judge gave little *weight* to that testimony.
He threw his *weight* behind the new proposal.

senses.gloss: The health, safety, and general well-being of a person or group.
examples: The school is responsible for the *welfare* of its students.
Child *welfare* workers visited the home twice.
Animal *welfare* groups protested the new law.

senses.gloss: A raised red mark left on the skin by a blow or a sting.
examples: The belt left *welts* across his back.
A mosquito bite raised a *welt* on her arm.
He had a *welt* under one eye after the fight.

senses.gloss: The round control a driver turns to steer a car.
examples: Don't text behind the *wheel*.
She took the *wheel* for the last hundred miles.
He fell asleep at the *wheel* and hit the guardrail.

senses.gloss: A member of a political party whose job is to keep other members voting with the party.
senses.ru: парламентский организатор партии (следит за дисциплиной голосования)
examples: The majority *whip* counted votes before the session.
Both *whips* said the bill would pass.
She served as party *whip* for six years.

senses.gloss: One of the hairs of a man's beard or the stubble on his face.
examples: Gray *whiskers* covered his chin.
He hadn't shaved, and the *whiskers* scratched her cheek.
A few white *whiskers* showed along his jaw.

senses.gloss: The high clear sound made by blowing through your lips or by a device.
examples: He let out a low *whistle* when he saw the price.
The *whistle* of the kettle woke everyone up.
We heard the train's *whistle* across the valley.

senses.gloss: The clear part of an egg, which turns white when cooked.
examples: Beat the egg *whites* until they hold a peak.
She eats only the *whites* and throws out the yolks.
Separate the *white* from the yolk carefully.

senses.gloss: The pale part of the eyeball around the colored center.
examples: The *whites* of his eyes were red from the smoke.
Yellow in the *whites* can be a sign of liver trouble.
She rolled her eyes until only the *whites* showed.

senses.gloss: The power of the mind to decide on something and keep going.
examples: She has the *will* to finish whatever she starts.
After the accident he lost the *will* to live.
It takes real *will* to train that early every day.

senses.gloss: What a person or a group wants to happen.
examples: The senator said he was following the *will* of the voters.
She was kept there against her *will*.
The board imposed its *will* on the whole department.

senses.gloss: The ability to breathe normally, especially during hard effort.
examples: The fall knocked the *wind* out of me.
Give me a second to get my *wind* back.
He found his second *wind* on the last mile.

senses.gloss: A separate area on a computer screen showing one program or file.
examples: Open the file in a new *window*.
I had six *windows* open and lost track of them.
Drag the *window* over to the second monitor.

senses.gloss: A limited period of time in which something can be done.
examples: The cable guy gave me a four-hour *window*.
There's a short *window* to file an appeal.
We missed our *window* to book cheap tickets.

senses.gloss: The outer end of a bird's wing or an airplane's wing.
examples: The plane's *wingtip* clipped a light pole.
Red lights blink at each *wingtip*.
The eagle's *wingtips* spread out like fingers.

senses.gloss: A promise that you will do something.
examples: You have my *word* that it stays between us.
He's a man of his *word*.
She gave me her *word* and then broke it.

senses.gloss: News or a message about something.
examples: *Word* came that the flight was canceled.
Send *word* as soon as you land.
There's still no *word* from the hospital.

senses.gloss: A short conversation with someone.
examples: Can I have a *word* with you?
The coach had a quiet *word* with the rookie.
A quick *word* before you head out?

senses.gloss: A bee or ant that gathers food and cares for the colony but does not breed.
examples: The *workers* feed the queen and the young.
A single *worker* can visit hundreds of flowers a day.
Most of the ants you see on the ground are *workers*.

senses.gloss: A harmful program that copies itself from computer to computer over a network.
examples: A *worm* shut down the hospital's network for two days.
The *worm* spread through email attachments.
Security teams patched the hole the *worm* used.

senses.gloss: A parasite that lives in the gut of a person or an animal.
examples: The puppy has *worms* and needs medicine.
Every child in the village was treated for *worms*.
The vet checks a stool sample for *worms*.

senses.gloss: The amount of something that a stated sum of money buys or a stated time uses.
examples: He put twenty dollars' *worth* of gas in the truck.
We have a week's *worth* of food in the pantry.
She bought a year's *worth* of contact lenses.

senses.gloss: Thin material such as plastic or paper used to cover food or gifts.
examples: Cover the bowl with plastic *wrap*.
We ran out of gift *wrap* on Christmas Eve.
Bubble *wrap* kept the glasses from breaking.

senses.gloss: The end of filming on a movie or a scene.
examples: The director called it a *wrap* at midnight.
That's a *wrap* on season three.
The cast had a *wrap* party on Friday.

senses.gloss: A person who is exhausted or badly upset.
examples: I was a nervous *wreck* before the interview.
After three nights with the baby, he's a *wreck*.
She's been a *wreck* since the funeral.

senses.gloss: A small fold or crease in cloth or paper.
examples: Hang the shirt up to keep the *wrinkles* out.
She smoothed the *wrinkles* from the tablecloth.
A hot iron takes out most *wrinkles*.

senses.gloss: A new detail or small problem that changes a situation.
examples: The lawsuit added a *wrinkle* to the deal.
There's one *wrinkle*: the seller wants cash.
Every case has its own *wrinkles*.

senses.gloss: A unit of length equal to three feet, about 0.91 meters.
examples: The store sells fabric by the *yard*.
He ran for eighty *yards* on the first play.
Give me another *yard* of rope.

senses.gloss: An enclosed outdoor area where a business stores goods or works on them.
examples: The lumber *yard* opens at seven.
Freight cars sat in the rail *yard* all week.
They keep the trucks in a fenced *yard* behind the shop.

senses.gloss: A long story told for entertainment, often hard to believe.
examples: Grandpa spun a *yarn* about a bear on the porch.
It's a good *yarn*, but I don't believe a word of it.
The old sailors traded *yarns* late into the night.

senses.gloss: A strong desire or longing for something.
examples: She had a *yen* for the ocean after years inland.
I've got a *yen* for something sweet.
His *yen* to travel never went away.

senses.gloss: The income an investment produces, usually given as a percentage.
examples: The bond has a *yield* of about four percent.
Falling rates pushed *yields* down all year.
Savers chase the highest *yield* they can find.

senses.gloss: A wooden frame joining two work animals at the neck so they pull together.
examples: The oxen pulled the plow under a heavy wooden *yoke*.
He lifted the *yoke* off the tired pair.
The *yoke* had rubbed sores into their necks.

senses.gloss: Harsh control by another country or ruler.
examples: The country threw off the *yoke* of colonial rule.
They lived for years under the *yoke* of a dictator.
Poets wrote about breaking the *yoke* of tyranny.

senses.gloss: Great enjoyment and energy for something.
examples: She has a real *zest* for life.
He attacked the job with *zest*.
Age hasn't dulled his *zest* for a good argument.

senses.gloss: A state of easy, complete focus in which you perform at your best.
examples: He was in the *zone* and hit every shot.
Once I'm in the *zone*, hours go by without my noticing.
She got in the *zone* and finished the draft in one night.
